The site is well positioned for road and rail transport, being in a major port with well-established road and rail infrastructure. However, the size of many major pieces of equipment, primarily the insulated storage tanks, precludes them from road and rail movements as pre-assembled units. As a result, it is recommended to make use of the excellent marine transportation links offered by the site and bring in the majority of equipment by sea. There is currently no berth immediately adjacent to the site; the marine berth intended to be used for the CO ship is shifted too far to the west to be used in site construction. 2 And an infrequently used LPG pipeline borders the northern edge of the site close to the water’s edge, creating a critical obstacle. Overcoming these two challenges is addressed in the following sections where a construction sequence is provided outlining what additional facilities would be required to integrate marine loading facilities into the overall construction plan. Installation will be sequential and aligned with a procurement plan to ensure the plant to be installed efficiently and as per schedule. Based upon the assessment conducted, the base case of marine transportation should be retained. Bringing in materials / equipment as pre-built multiple units along with specific large scale vessel builds straight to and traveling into the site has considerable advantages. As an alternative to large on-site fabrications, this utilization of a remote build concept allow works to be undertaken within controlled Page93 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version factory / workshop environments, in steady state conditions, enabling good productivity levels, quality work control and safety hazard reductions. To facilitate this, the engineering design should be developed to include an extensive element of modularization, thus simplifying the on-site installations, minimizing a number of construction high-risk activities such as extensive working at height and large welding scopes. Modularization of the packages by size and weight, with ease of interconnections, will determine and optimize the transportation as well as construction methods, notwithstanding any road/rail transport constraints. Having equipment / packages assembled in modular type prefabrication builds at subcontractors offsite yards provides for a number of advantages e.g. reductions on multiple transport, as well as the sequential build schedule opportunities, further simplifying site installations and reducing on-site specialist trades resources. Pre-build modularization aids the overall schedule by allowing more time for civil ground works since module foundations would need to be fully completed prior to construction commencement. In planning terms, the early phase works such as the metering and utility packages can be completed while pre- fabrications are being built off-site. That can proceed in parallel, rather than sequentially if these large- scale fabrications were to be assembled on-site.
